messages.content: How do I interop with JavaScript objects and functions in ClojureScript?

ClojureScript provides seamless JavaScript interoperability: ```clojure ;; Call JS functions (js/alert "Hello from CLJS!") (js/console.log "Debug message") ;; Access JS properties with .- (.-length "hello") ; => 5 (.-innerText element) ;; Set JS properties with set! (set! (.-innerHTML element) "Bold") ;; Call JS methods with . (.toUpperCase "hello") ; => "HELLO" (.getElementById js/document "app") ;; Create JS objects (js-obj "foo" 1 "bar" 2) ; => {foo: 1, bar: 2} (clj->js {:foo 1 :bar 2}) ; => {foo: 1, bar: 2} ;; Convert JS to Clojure (js->clj js-object) ; shallow (js->clj js-object :keywordize-keys true) ; with keywords ;; Access nested properties (.. js/window -location -href) (aget js-array 0) ; array access ;; Call with apply (.apply js/Math.max nil #js [1 2 3]) ; => 3 ;; Use js* for raw JS (escape hatch) (js* "new Date()") ``` Prefer ClojureScript data structures internally and convert at JS boundaries.
What build tools are available for ClojureScript and how do they compare?

The main ClojureScript build tools:

**1. Shadow-cljs (Recommended for web)**
```clojure
;; shadow-cljs.edn
{:source-paths ["src"]
 :dependencies [[reagent "1.2.0"]]
 :builds {:app {:target :browser
               :output-dir "public/js"
               :asset-path "/js"
               :modules {:main {:init-fn app.core/init}}}}}

;; Commands
;; npx shadow-cljs watch app    - dev with hot reload
;; npx shadow-cljs release app  - production build
```

**2. Figwheel-main**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {com.bhauman/figwheel-main {:mvn/version "0.2.18"}}
 :paths ["src" "resources"]}

;; dev.cljs.edn
{:main app.core}

;; clj -M -m figwheel.main -b dev -r
```

**3. ClojureScript Compiler (Direct)**
```clojure
;; build.clj
(require '[cljs.build.api :as b])
(b/build "src"
  {:main 'app.core
   :output-to "out/main.js"
   :optimizations :advanced})
```

**Comparison:**
| Feature | Shadow-cljs | Figwheel | Direct |
|---------|-------------|----------|--------|
| NPM Integration | Excellent | Good | Manual |
| Hot Reload | Built-in | Built-in | No |
| Config | EDN | EDN | Clojure |
| REPL | Yes | Yes | Yes |

Shadow-cljs is recommended for most projects due to its npm integration.
How do I work with the DOM in ClojureScript without React?

Direct DOM manipulation in ClojureScript: ```clojure (ns app.dom (:require [goog.dom :as gdom] [goog.events :as gevents])) ;; Query elements (def app-el (gdom/getElement "app")) (def items (gdom/getElementsByClass "item")) (def first-p (gdom/getElementByTagNameAndClass "p" "intro")) ;; Create elements (def new-div (gdom/createElement "div")) (gdom/setTextContent new-div "Hello!") (gdom/appendChild app-el new-div) ;; Modify elements (gdom/setProperties new-div #js {:id "greeting" :class "message"}) (set! (.-innerHTML new-div) "Bold text") ;; Remove elements (gdom/removeNode new-div) ;; Event handling (gevents/listen (gdom/getElement "btn") "click" (fn [e] (.preventDefault e) (js/console.log "Clicked!"))) ;; Using native APIs directly (-> js/document (.querySelector ".container") (.-classList) (.add "active")) ;; Template literals for HTML (set! (.-innerHTML container) (str "
    " (apply str (map #(str "
  • " % "
    • ") items)) "
")) ``` Google Closure library (`goog.*`) provides cross-browser utilities. For complex UIs, consider Reagent/React instead.
Explain ClojureScript advanced compilation and how to avoid issues with it.

Advanced compilation aggressively optimizes code but can break JS interop:

**The Problem:**
```clojure
;; This breaks under :advanced
(.-myProperty js-object)  ; renamed to e.g., .-a
(.myMethod js-object)     ; renamed to .b
```

**Solutions:**

**1. Externs files**
```javascript
// externs.js
var MyLibrary = {};
MyLibrary.myProperty;
MyLibrary.myMethod = function() {};
```
```clojure
;; In build config
{:optimizations :advanced
 :externs ["externs.js"]}
```

**2. String access (avoids renaming)**
```clojure
;; Use aget/aset for property access
(aget js-object "myProperty")
(aset js-object "myProperty" value)

;; Use goog.object for safety
(require '[goog.object :as gobj])
(gobj/get js-object "myProperty")
(gobj/set js-object "myProperty" value)
```

**3. ^js type hints**
```clojure
;; Type hint prevents renaming
(defn process-event [^js event]
  (.-target event)       ; preserved
  (.preventDefault event)) ; preserved

;; For return values
(defn get-element ^js [id]
  (js/document.getElementById id))
```

**4. Export your API**
```clojure
(defn ^:export my-public-fn [x]
  (* x 2))
;; Callable as: myns.my_public_fn(5)
```

**Best Practices:**
- Always use `^js` hints on JS objects
- Use npm modules via shadow-cljs (auto-externs)
- Test with `:advanced` before release
- Use `:pseudo-names true` for debugging
How do I manage state in ClojureScript applications?

State management options in ClojureScript:

**1. Atoms (Simple local state)**
```clojure
(def app-state (atom {:count 0 :items []}))

;; Read
@app-state  ; => {:count 0 :items []}

;; Update
(swap! app-state update :count inc)
(swap! app-state assoc :items [1 2 3])

;; Watch for changes
(add-watch app-state :logger
  (fn [key atom old-state new-state]
    (js/console.log "State changed:" (clj->js new-state))))
```

**2. Reagent atoms (Reactive)**
```clojure
(require '[reagent.core :as r])

(def counter (r/atom 0))

;; Components re-render when dereferenced atoms change
(defn counter-display []
  [:div "Count: " @counter])

;; Cursors for sub-state
(def items (r/cursor app-state [:items]))
```

**3. Re-frame (Complex apps)**
```clojure
;; Centralized app-db
(rf/reg-event-db :increment
  (fn [db _]
    (update db :count inc)))

(rf/reg-sub :count
  (fn [db _]
    (:count db)))

;; In component
(let [count @(rf/subscribe [:count])]
  [:button {:on-click #(rf/dispatch [:increment])}
   count])
```

**4. DataScript (In-memory DB)**
```clojure
(require '[datascript.core :as d])

(def schema {:person/friends {:db/valueType :db.type/ref
                              :db/cardinality :db.cardinality/many}})
(def conn (d/create-conn schema))

(d/transact! conn [{:person/name "Alice" :person/age 30}])
(d/q '[:find ?n :where [?e :person/name ?n]] @conn)
```

Choose based on complexity: Atoms → Reagent atoms → Re-frame → DataScript
How do I make HTTP requests in ClojureScript?

HTTP requests in ClojureScript:

**1. Using cljs-ajax (Popular library)**
```clojure
(require '[ajax.core :refer [GET POST PUT DELETE]])

;; GET request
(GET "/api/users"
  {:handler       (fn [response] (js/console.log response))
   :error-handler (fn [error] (js/console.error error))
   :response-format :json
   :keywords? true})

;; POST with data
(POST "/api/users"
  {:params {:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}
   :format :json
   :handler #(js/console.log "Created:" %)})
```

**2. Using Fetch API directly**
```clojure
(defn fetch-data [url]
  (-> (js/fetch url)
      (.then #(.json %))
      (.then #(js->clj % :keywordize-keys true))
      (.catch #(js/console.error "Error:" %))))

;; With options
(defn post-data [url data]
  (-> (js/fetch url
        #js {:method "POST"
             :headers #js {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
             :body (js/JSON.stringify (clj->js data))})
      (.then #(.json %))))
```

**3. With core.async**
```clojure
(require '[cljs.core.async :refer [go <!]]
         '[cljs-http.client :as http])

(go
  (let [response (<! (http/get "/api/users"))]
    (if (= 200 (:status response))
      (process-users (:body response))
      (handle-error response))))

;; POST
(go
  (let [response (<! (http/post "/api/users"
                       {:json-params {:name "Alice"}}))]
    (js/console.log (:body response))))
```

**4. Re-frame http-fx (with Re-frame)**
```clojure
(require '[day8.re-frame.http-fx])

(rf/reg-event-fx :fetch-users
  (fn [_ _]
    {:http-xhrio {:method :get
                  :uri "/api/users"
                  :response-format (ajax/json-response-format {:keywords? true})
                  :on-success [:users-loaded]
                  :on-failure [:http-error]}}))
```
How do I use NPM packages in ClojureScript?

Using NPM packages in ClojureScript (via Shadow-cljs):

**1. Install packages**
```bash
npm install react react-dom lodash axios
```

**2. Require in ClojureScript**
```clojure
(ns app.core
  (:require
    ;; Default export
    ["axios" :as axios]
    
    ;; Named exports
    ["lodash/map" :as lodash-map]
    ["lodash" :as _ :refer [debounce throttle]]
    
    ;; React
    ["react" :as react]
    ["react-dom/client" :as react-dom]))

;; Use axios
(-> (axios/get "/api/data")
    (.then #(js/console.log (.-data %))))

;; Use lodash
(debounce #(js/console.log "debounced") 300)
(lodash-map #js [1 2 3] inc)

;; ES6 classes
(ns app.editor
  (:require ["codemirror" :as CodeMirror]))

(def editor (CodeMirror. element #js {:lineNumbers true}))
```

**3. shadow-cljs.edn configuration**
```clojure
{:source-paths ["src"]
 :dependencies [[reagent "1.2.0"]]
 :builds
 {:app
  {:target :browser
   :output-dir "public/js"
   :modules {:main {:init-fn app.core/init}}
   ;; NPM resolve options
   :js-options {:resolve {"lodash" {:target :npm
                                     :require "lodash-es"}}}
   ;; Include npm deps in bundle
   :devtools {:after-load app.core/reload}}}}
```

**4. React components**
```clojure
;; Using React component from npm
(ns app.ui
  (:require ["@material-ui/core/Button" :default Button]
            [reagent.core :as r]))

(defn my-button []
  [:> Button {:variant "contained" :color "primary"}
   "Click me"])
```

Shadow-cljs handles npm integration seamlessly - no externs needed!
How do I set up routing in a ClojureScript SPA?

Client-side routing in ClojureScript:

**1. Using Reitit (Recommended)**
```clojure
(ns app.router
  (:require [reitit.frontend :as rf]
            [reitit.frontend.easy :as rfe]
            [reitit.coercion.spec :as rss]
            [reagent.core :as r]))

(def routes
  [["/" {:name :home
         :view home-page}]
   ["/users" {:name :users
              :view users-page}]
   ["/users/:id" {:name :user
                  :view user-page
                  :parameters {:path {:id int?}}}]])

(defonce match (r/atom nil))

(defn init-router! []
  (rfe/start!
    (rf/router routes {:data {:coercion rss/coercion}})
    (fn [m] (reset! match m))
    {:use-fragment true}))  ; or false for HTML5 history

;; Navigation
(rfe/href :home)              ; => "#/"
(rfe/href :user {:id 42})     ; => "#/users/42"
(rfe/push-state :users)       ; navigate programmatically

;; Current route view
(defn app []
  (if-let [view (-> @match :data :view)]
    [view @match]
    [:div "404 - Page not found"]))
```

**2. With Re-frame**
```clojure
(rf/reg-event-fx :navigate
  (fn [_ [_ route params]]
    {:navigate! [route params]}))

(rf/reg-fx :navigate!
  (fn [[route params]]
    (rfe/push-state route params)))

(rf/reg-event-db :set-route
  (fn [db [_ match]]
    (assoc db :route match)))

;; Initialize
(defn init-router! []
  (rfe/start!
    (rf/router routes)
    #(rf/dispatch [:set-route %])
    {:use-fragment false}))
```

**3. Route guards/middleware**
```clojure
(def routes
  [["/admin" {:name :admin
              :view admin-page
              :middleware [auth-middleware]}]
   ["/public" {:name :public
               :view public-page}]])

(defn auth-middleware [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (if (authenticated?)
      (handler request)
      (rfe/push-state :login))))
```
